There are no suspicious network operations, obfuscated code, or unexpected system modifications in the global scope or `pkgver()` function.

The `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` commands will only download and extract the verified source tarball, which is exactly what's needed for auditing. No code will execute during this gate beyond fetching and extraction of the verified archive.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for isc-stork-server.service:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a systemd service unit for the ISC Stork Server. It contains standard service configuration directives: Description, Documentation, dependency ordering (Wants/After for network-online.target and time-sync.target), service user (stork-server), ExecStart pointing to the stork-server binary, ExecReload sending SIGHUP, an EnvironmentFile reference, and restart-on-failure behavior. The service is enabled under multi-user.target.

All directives present are conventional systemd unit options consistent with a typical server daemon service file. There are no suspicious commands, no network download/exec patterns (curl/wget/eval/base64 are absent), no obfuscated content, and no operations targeting unrelated system files or data exfiltration paths. The EnvironmentFile path (/etc/stork/server.env) and ConfigurationDirectory=stork usage are normal for application configuration, and the ExecStart/ExecReload values align with the application's stated purpose as a server daemon. While the service runs as a dedicated unprivileged user (stork-server) rather than root, this is standard practice and does not introduce a supply-chain risk.</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard systemd unit for Stork server daemon</summary>
</security_assessment>
